mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital and stimulates equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annual inflation rate above 2.5% (measured by CPIAUCSL) signals potential monetary tightening and reduced equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL annual change exceeds 2.5% over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1.5% and the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, the combination signals a stimulative monetary policy coupled with a weak labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1.5% and UNRATE > 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market boom (HOUST > 1300), strong housing activity signals robust consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1300 over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 105 over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is above 2% and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300, the combination signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 > 2% and HOUST > 1300 over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%), a federal funds rate below 1.5% indicates insufficient monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.5% over a 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
